statement: Two of the ten users routes are registered without an authorization context on the handler: admin_list_all_users and admin_get_user take no AdminClaims extension, while fifty sibling admin handlers do, so those handlers cannot apply any per-caller or per-tenant rule even where the route middleware authenticates the request.
evidence: code: admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:4394-4400 (list signature, no claims), :4469-4473 (get signature, no claims); contrast admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:789-794, :4505-4510 (claims present); route registration admin/backend/src/main.rs:255-286

statement: The panel offers a role the server refuses: the SPA's role list for a super_admin includes super_admin itself, while the server's assignable set excludes it and answers 400 Invalid platform role.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:11-12 (ROLES and ALL_ROLES incl. super_admin) and :85 (availableRoles = isSuperAdmin ? ALL_ROLES : ROLES); server set admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:869 (ADMIN_ASSIGNABLE_ROLES) with the refusal at :873-875

statement: One enum, three sources: the SPA's assignable list, its colour map, and the server's assignable set each enumerate roles independently, and the colour map carries a key the assignable list does not.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:11-12 (two lists), :14-16 (roleColors with five keys incl. super_admin and admin), admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:869 (four roles)

statement: The committed technical reference lists five of the admin routes while the router registers seventy-four under the same prefix, so the document cannot serve as the capability contract a diff would need.
evidence: code: docs/core/technical-reference.md:1002-1005 (five route rows) against admin/backend/src/main.rs (74 occurrences of "/api/v1/admin/")

where: aibim users list vs its own contract
statement: The route is documented as paginated and implements limit/offset/search with a default of 50 and a clamp of 500, while the surface requests a fixed limit of 200, renders no pager, and presents the fetched page as the whole population in its header and its four stat cards.
evidence: code: admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:4399-4416 (limit default 50, clamp 1-500, offset, search) against admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:44-47 (limit: 200), :95 ("N users across all tenants"), :101-104 (stats over that page)

statement: Two write paths for one entity validate differently: the role change uses a typed body with unknown-field rejection and a length check, while create and update parse a raw JSON value with silent defaults, so a missing role becomes viewer and an e-mail is accepted with no format check.
evidence: code: admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:795-800 (typed UserRoleUpdateReq validate) against :892-905 (create parses serde_json::Value with unwrap_or defaults) and :4505-4520 (update does the same, no validation)

where: aibim users list state after a mutation
statement: After a role or status change the surface patches the selected record locally and invalidates the list query, so the dependent rows are recomputed rather than left stale; the stat cards and the header count are recomputed from the same query.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:65-72 (role mutation patch + invalidateQueries), :73-82 (status mutation), :101-104 (stats derived from the query)

statement: The deactivate and activate routes carry no role check beyond the route middleware, which admits admin and super_admin, and the surface renders the control for every panel user: the two sides agree, so this row records a covered case.
evidence: code: admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:835-870 (no role check past claims), admin/backend/src/middleware.rs (require_admin_access admits the platform admin role), admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:207-215 (control rendered without a role gate)

statement: Search is server-side: the surface debounces 250 ms and passes the term as a query parameter the handler binds into its filtered query, and the empty state is rendered from the returned list. The two layers agree.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:37-47 (debounce + search param), admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:4406-4416 (search bound to LIST_FILTERED), admin/frontend/src/api/admin.ts:374-377

statement: The two destructive mutations on this screen - deactivate and role change - fire directly from the detail panel with no confirmation step, and the surface ships no confirmation component to reuse, so the record about to lose access is never shown before the act.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:207-215 (button calls the mutation), :65-72 (role change calls the mutation); a search of admin/frontend/src for a Confirm component returns none

statement: The users area has no multi-step flow: creation is one modal and it posts the whole record in one request, so the flow-prerequisite class has no instance on this feature.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:243-270 (single create modal, one mutation), admin/frontend/src/api/admin.ts:383-387 (one POST)

where: the analysis artifact (same slot row as the first feature)
statement: Every fix for A01-A06 names a layer that exists but is unused or a rule the contract does not carry: a claims extractor on two handlers, a shared role vocabulary, a regenerated route table, a typed body on both write paths, pagination state in the surface. The artifact the analysis follows has no section in which that infrastructure change is proposed.

statement: The create form submits with any field empty (the button is disabled only while a request is in flight) and the handler fills every missing value from a default, so a record can be created with an empty email, an empty password and a viewer role; the only password policy in the codebase lives in the CLI binary, not on this path.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:257-266 (submit enabled with empty fields), admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:892-905 (unwrap_or defaults for email, password, full_name, role), contrast admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:869 (a role allow-list exists on the other write path)

statement: The app ships a Pager in its own component library and the users route paginates server-side, while the users surface imports no pager and requests a fixed page size: a capability that exists in the product and is unreachable on the surface that needs it.
evidence: code: admin/frontend/src/components/ui/Pager.tsx exists; admin/frontend/src/pages/Users.tsx:6 (import list has no Pager), :44-47 (fixed limit 200); route pagination admin/backend/src/handlers/admin.rs:4399-4416
